fact: The National Council for Persons with Disabilities and IDI Uganda, with KOICA funding, set up an ICT hub in Kasese that will provide computer literacy and vocational digital training to persons with disabilities and the wider community.

The Ministry of ICT and National Guidance, with MTN Foundation Uganda and Centenary Technology Services, is implementing a Shs4 billion, three-year programme of four regional digital innovation hubs at public universities plus the Nakawa hub, expected to give over 20,000 students and community members digital skills training; the second hub was handed over at Busitema University.

fact: UCC, through UCUSAF, reports programme records for 2020-2026 of more than 13,000 women and over 11,000 rural community participants trained in digital skills, and more than 5,000 MSMEs.

The Ministry of ICT and National Guidance's Permanent Secretary says over 10,000 Ugandans have learned digital skills through government programmes, including the DigiTruck mobile classroom in Kasese, Kabale, Lira, Soroti and Hoima.

The Gender, Labour and Social Development ministry, with Huawei, runs the Digi-Truck mobile classroom project launched in March 2023, which had benefited 8,192 Ugandans by September 2025, including 350 graduating in Amuria district on 5 September 2025.
A UCC-commissioned assessment says UCUSAF ran a Digital Literacy for Girls and Women project and digital skilling under the ICT4PWD programme, with no count of people trained given.
